newsitem.title: UK: Paper Brent dips, spreads, CFDs weaker.
newsitem.headline: Paper Brent dips, spreads, CFDs weaker.

text.p: North Sea Brent easied on Tuesday on a quiet paper market, traders said.
No physical Brent deals were reported early with most European traders returning to work after Monday's Pentecost holiday.

A June 4-6 Flotta was reported to have changed hands at Dated Brent -77 cents, some 25 cents firmer than the last trade. Fixed freight Norwegian grades were also steady with the current high freigh rates in Northwest Europe, traders said. Dated Brent was assessed at July Brent -20/25 cents, steady to a little easier than Monday's July Brent -20 cents deal.
"We are looking for interest but we haven't seen any this morning, no fresh bids," a trader with a June 2-4 Brent on offer said. "We will try to do dated related."
In an equally quiet paper market, one July Brent outright was traded at $20, or 26-27 cents weaker than its trade levels in the U.S. aftermarket.
On the IPE, July Brent was 21 cents a barrel down at $19.95 by 1229 GMT.
Poor refinery margins which could result in poor crude demand were largely behind the fall, coupled with fears of a pre-expiry jump on June NYMEX crude, traders said.
Brent intermonth spreads eased, with Jun/Jul very thinly talked at -5/0 cents from 1/3 cents late on Monday and Jul/Aug offered five cents lower at -2 cents.
Brent contracts for difference also weakened in thin talk, with next week's, June 2-6 and June 9-13 offered four to five cents weaker at July Brent -25 cents.
The only CFD reported traded was a June 12-18 at August -26 cents, or the equivalent of July -22 cents.
One Brent was in the chains, a cargo five o'clocked on Friday that won a deferral.
Other North Sea grades were also thinly talked.
One Norwegian major seller starting to show early June grades but no bids have been made yet.
The company also said it had two unsold May cargoes on offer, an Ekofisk at Dated Brent +15/20 cents, a little easier than its earlier levels, and an Oseberg whose price was negotiable.
There was unconfirmed talk of an end May Ekofisk co-loaded on Monday by a trading house and a Wall Street trader at Dated Brent -5 cents, some 25 cents off its current levels.
A Gullfaks cargo was reported sold recently but no further details were available.

Traders said that fixed freight Norwegian grades like Statfjord, which traded twice at a 33 cents premium to Dated Brent on Monday, and Gullfaks were popular at the moment because of high freight rates due to a shortage in loading vessels.
"But by about June 5-10 that benefit will have eroded," one trader said, adding that he expected the freight rates to come down soon.
On the West African market, Ghana refiner Tema on Monday awarded a tender to Elf to supply two cargoes of 450,000 barrels of Bonny Light at Dated Brent +59 cents.
Tema also awarded Glencore two cargoes of 450,000 barrels of Brass River at Dated +89 cents.
Traders assessed Bonny Light at around Dated +50 cents, some three cents firmer.
The high price for the Tema tender was the result of a small cargo premium for smaller parcels charged by Nigeria's NNPC. Berthing facilites at the refinery can only take the smaller vessels.
Forcados was seen around five cents higher at Dated +20 cents.
The Mediterranean had a quiet start to the week after the Monday Pentecost holiday, with benchmark Brent's strength continuing to inspire buyer caution.
Russian sour Urals was assessed at Dated -$1.10 for smaller parcels and around Dated -$1.00 for the larger parcels.

But one trader said he thought refineries could pick up cargoes at Dated -$1.20, some five cents below last week's traded levels. None of the four end May barrels offered on Monday appeared to have been taken, traders said.
"We're all waiting for prices to come down,' a trader said. "There is not much buying with refinery margins being so poor."
-H. Haddadin, B. Maclean, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
